purpose: U30F F4 / U30F2 M4: a replace promote (retainOutgoingThenReplace, phase B) holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the target for one interactive transaction of transaction_timeout_ms. Under that lock it waits for the lock, computes digests_under_lock full-table digests, then TRUNCATEs the target and INSERTs every incoming row. For a target listed here, the promote and the retention backfill are refused until a MEASURED entry (reviewed commit) records measured_digest_seconds (ONE digest, the larger of live and retained) AND measured_replace_seconds (the TRUNCATE + INSERT of measured_rows rows), and digests_under_lock x measured_digest_seconds + measured_replace_seconds fits within lock_budget_fraction of the timeout; the rest of the timeout is headroom for the unmeasured lock wait, small reads/writes and load. A digest time alone never meets it. The timeout is also the promote transaction's timeout (import-librarian-manifest reads it from here) and is not raised to make a measurement fit. There is no runtime override.

env.registerenhetsomradesytor.reason: Property layer, about 4.4 M rows (U20-U30-SPEC). The verifier's estimate (PGlite 124 us/row, native 2-4x faster, larger EWKB) puts one digest at 2-9 minutes, so two digests under the exclusive lock likely exceed the budget on their own, before the TRUNCATE + INSERT of the same 4.4 M rows that runs under the same lock; every read of the table is blocked meanwhile. Not measured. Digest time (owner-approved, read-only, likely > 5 minutes): retain-spatial-dataset-versions --measure-digest --target env.registerenhetsomradesytor, recording its measured_digest_seconds. measured_replace_seconds (TRUNCATE + INSERT of the same rows into a copy with the same indexes, never on live) is measured by no tool here. With the committed numbers the budget is 300 s: 2 x digest + replace <= 300 s; a digest above 150 s alone means the digest-under-lock design must change (owner decision) before the first real promote or backfill of this layer.
